# Proverbs 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Like-snow in-summer and-like-rain in-harvest, so honor [is]-not fitting for-a-fool.

**2** Like-a-sparrow for-wandering, like-a-swallow for-flying, so a-curse without-cause does-not-come.

**3** A-whip for-[the]-horse, a-bridle for-[the]-donkey, and-a-rod for-[the]-back-of fools.

**4** Do-not-answer a-fool according-to his-folly, lest you-be-equal — even you — to-him.

**5** Answer a-fool according-to his-folly, lest he-be wise in-his-[own]-eyes.

**6** Cutting-off feet, drinking violence — one-sending messages by-[the]-hand-of a-fool.

**7** Legs hang-limp from-[the]-lame, and-[so is] a-proverb in-[the]-mouth-of fools.

**8** Like-one-binding a-stone in-a-sling, so [is]-one-giving honor to-a-fool.

**9** A-thorn goes-up into-[the]-hand-of a-drunkard, and-[so is] a-proverb in-[the]-mouth-of fools.

**10** An-archer wounding everyone — so [is one]-hiring a-fool and-hiring [those]-passing-by.

**11** Like-a-dog returning to-his-vomit — a-fool repeating his-folly.

**12** You-see a-man wise in-his-[own]-eyes — more hope for-a-fool than-for-him.

**13** [The]-sluggard says, 'A-lion [is] in-the-road! A-lion [is] between the-plazas!'

**14** [The]-door turns upon its-hinge, and-[the]-sluggard upon his-bed.

**15** [The]-sluggard buries his-hand in-the-dish; he-is-too-weary to-return-it to his-mouth.

**16** [The]-sluggard [is]-wiser in-his-[own]-eyes than-seven [men who]-return a-sensible-answer.

**17** One-seizing [the]-ears-of a-dog [who]-passes-by — one-becoming-enraged over a-quarrel not-his-own.

**18** Like-a-madman shooting firebrands, arrows, and-death,

**19** So [is] a-man [who]-deceives his-neighbor and-says, 'Was-I-not joking?'

**20** For-lack-of wood a-fire goes-out, and-where-there-is-no whisperer strife is-quieted.

**21** Charcoal for-embers and-wood for-fire, and-a-man-of contentions to-kindle strife.

**22** [The]-words-of a-whisperer [are]-like-dainty-morsels, and-they go-down into-[the]-chambers-of [the]-belly.

**23** Silver-of dross overlaid upon earthenware — lips burning and-a-heart evil.

**24** With-his-lips [the]-one-hating disguises-himself, but-in-his-inner-being he-sets deceit.

**25** When-he-makes-gracious his-voice do-not-trust-him, for seven abominations [are] in-his-heart.

**26** Hatred covers-itself with-deception; his-evil will-be-revealed in-[the]-assembly.

**27** One-digging a-pit — into-it he-will-fall, and-one-rolling a-stone — upon-him it-will-return.

**28** A-tongue lying hates its-crushed-ones, and-a-mouth smooth makes ruin.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **26:4-5**: The famous contradictory pair — placed deliberately side by side. Meta-wisdom: the right response depends on the situation. This is not error but pedagogy.

- **26:11**: Kelev shav al-qe'o — 'a dog returning to its vomit.' Cited in 2 Peter 2:22. Vivid, unforgettable image of cyclical foolishness.

- **26:23**: Keseph sigim — 'silver of dross' or possibly 'glaze.' The metaphor: attractive surface hiding corrupt interior. Deception in its purest form.

— EMET
